title: Narration adds what the picture can't
statement: Make each narration line add what the picture cannot show, rather than describe what the frame already makes obvious.
detail: The language rules of an intro-video BrainLift for a Grade 3 reading course say narration must add what the frame cannot say and must not describe facts already obvious in the same frame, and a line that captions its own picture is rejected (`downloads/BrainLift - What makes a good intro video.md`, lines 943 and 145). Its line test pairs a shot of an animal sweeping an underground room with a line about how tired he had grown of cleaning his home (line 939). Naming what is on screen counts as adding, because a scene of two animals reads as two animals, not as the characters, unless somebody says so (line 319); and the read-along rules keep each line inside its shot, saying nothing the shot does not show (line 957). What a line can add includes a thought, a cause or the name for what is on screen.
